raw:
The morning mist coils through the high windows of the Massassi temple, carrying the cool, green smell of Yavin 4’s jungle. Luke Skywalker stands a few paces away, his silhouette still against the fading stars. He looks as though he hasn’t moved all night. When you finally speak, your voice feels too loud in the hush.

“Master Skywalker… what’s beneath the temple? And is Kira drawn to it?”

Luke turns to you, his eyes clear but weighed by something old. He doesn’t answer at once. The silence is warm and patient, yet it prickles against your skin like the memory of that buried pressure.

“Something the Massassi tried to seal away,” he says at last. “A vergence—old, hungry, and not of the light. It’s been sleeping a long time. But it’s waking now.” His gaze settles on you, not accusing, simply certain. “You felt it. So has Kira.”

You swallow, and the memory comes unwanted: that cold, knowing presence turning its attention on you like an eye opening in the dark.

“Kira’s been studying the old Massassi glyphs in the lower archive,” Luke continues. “She told me she found mention of a sealed passage beneath the eastern foundation. I’ve never located it. She may have.”

He doesn’t say more. He doesn’t need to.

“Her path is her own,” Luke says softly. “I can’t walk it for her, and neither can you. But remember—the dark side isn’t just a trap. It’s a mirror. It shows you the self that craves power, answers, control. If you follow her, you’ll face your own reflection.”

A chill crawls up your spine, worse than the dawn cold. You remember how near you came to accepting that easy clarity, how sweet it had seemed. The thing beneath the temple noticed you. And for a heartbeat, you let it.

Luke rests a hand on your shoulder, the touch brief but grounding. “The Force won’t give you simple answers. Only the strength to choose well.”

He steps back, leaving you alone with the choice—and the fear.

---CHOICES---
1. Slip down to the lower archive and examine the Massassi glyphs Kira was studying for any clue to the sealed passage. [Perception]
2. Sit with the discomfort and meditate, reaching out carefully with your senses to understand the vergence’s pull on Kira without drawing its attention again. [Force:Sense]
3. Search the Praxeum’s central library for any record Master Yoda or the old Jedi left about buried dark-side vergences and how they were contained. [Vigilance]

Draft:
The air in the Massassi temple is cool and thick with the scent of ancient stone and damp jungle. Mist coils outside the open windows, silver in the first true light of dawn. Luke Skywalker stands motionless, his robes still, his eyes half-closed as if listening to something far away. You take a breath, feeling the faint echo of that buried heat still prickling at the back of your mind.

“Master Skywalker,” you say, your voice smaller than you intend, “what is beneath the temple? And... is Kira drawn to it?”

Luke opens his eyes. They are clear and blue, but shadowed by something you can’t name. He doesn’t answer for a long moment. Then he steps closer, his mechanical hand whirring softly.

“Something old was sealed down there,” he says at last. “The Massassi built this temple over a place of power, hoping to contain it. They failed in some ways. What remains doesn’t belong to the light.” He looks at you, not unkindly. “You felt it.”

It’s not a question. You nod, and the memory brings a chill that has nothing to do with the morning breeze.

“Kira’s path is her own,” Luke says. “I can’t walk it for her. Nor can you.” He pauses, and his gaze softens into something sad. “But I can tell you that she’s been spending time in the lower archive, among the old Massassi writings. She said she found a record of a sealed passage. I haven’t been able to open it.”

He places a hand on your shoulder. The touch is warm, but there’s a weight in it. “Be careful,” he says. “The dark side isn’t just temptation. It’s a mirror. It shows you yourself, twisted. That’s what she’s facing. And if you go looking for her, you’ll face it too.”

The words settle into your stomach like a stone. Suddenly you’re too aware of your own heartbeat, of the whisper of power that called to you earlier—and how close you came to answering.

Luke releases you and steps back. “Meditate on what you’ve sensed. The Force will guide you, if you let it.”

He doesn’t offer to help directly. The responsibility, you realize, is yours.

Word count: ~280. A bit long, need to trim. Actionable lead: lower archive, sealed passage record. Emotional complication: mirror of dark side, fear of facing twisted self. Trim details, compress.

“Master Skywalker—what’s under the temple? And is Kira drawn to it?”

He turns to you, his expression calm but weary. The silence stretches long before he answers. “Something the Massassi tried to bury. A vergence, old and hungry. It’s been quiet for centuries, but it’s waking.” His gaze doesn’t waver. “Yes, you felt it. So has Kira.”

You swallow. The memory of that cold, noticing pressure makes your skin prickle.

“Kira told me she’s been reading the old Massassi glyphs in the lower archive,” Luke continues. “She found mention of a sealed passage somewhere below the eastern foundation. I’ve never located it.” He pauses, letting the implication hang: Kira might have.

“I can’t make Kira’s choices for her, and I won’t.” Luke’s voice is gentle, but firm. “But remember—the dark side isn’t a monster under a rock. It’s a mirror. It shows you the version of yourself that wants everything. Power, answers, control. If you follow her path, you’ll see your own reflection there.”

A chill creeps up your spine, worse than the dawn cold. You recall how easy it had been to almost reach for clarity, how sweet the temptation felt. The thing beneath the temple had noticed you. And for a heartbeat, you’d let it.

Luke rests a hand on your shoulder. “Meditate on this. The Force gives us no simple answers, only the strength to choose well.” He steps back, leaving you with the weight of the decision.
